summary: Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~2002–2008) under supervisor Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper (1907–2003) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1926–1934) and held a post there from 1939 to 1972, succeeding Jean Philippe Vogel.

F. M. Hassnain (1924–2016) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of the Punjab (until ~1944) and served as Director of the Department of Archives, Archaeology & Museums, Government of Jammu and Kashmir (~1954–1983).
Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary (~1996–2001) under Leslie S. Kawamura. His students include Nirupam Chakma and Yong Hua Shi.

Fabienne Jagou (born 1964) specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She received her PhD from the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~1993–1999) and became a Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~2001).

Fabio Rambelli (born 1963) is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Massimo Raveri and Adriana Boscaro (~1985–1989). He served as an Associate Professor at Sapporo University (2001–2002).

Fabrizia Baldissera works in Indology. She studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004) and held posts at the University of Florence (~2002) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
Fafang (1904–1951) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu (~1922–1947). From ~1943 to 1946, he was a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-kuei Li (1902–1987) worked in linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1921–1924) and the University of Michigan (~1924–1926), later holding posts at Yale, Washington (~1949–1969), Hawaii (~1969–1973), and the University of Chicago.
Fausto Gherardo Fumi (1840–1915) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Giuseppe Bardelli at the Scuola Normale Superiore's Classe di Lettere e Filosofia from ~1858 to 1862.

Fazun (1902–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery. He served as director of the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (1934–1950) and the Buddhist Academy of China (1956–1980).

Fedde Maarten de Vries is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of California, Berkeley (~2013–2015), where Robert H. Sharf, Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and Alexander von Rospatt served on his committee.

Ferdinand Benary (1805–1880) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied under Franz Bopp (~1827–1829). In 1831, he became an associate professor in the theological faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin.

Ferdinand Diederich Lessing (1882–1961) worked in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1925–1935) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1935–1952).

Ferdinand Justi (1837–1907) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1854–1856) and under Theodor Benfey (~1856–1859), later serving on the faculty at Marburg (~1865–1907).

Ferdinand Sommer (1875–1962) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1893–1896). He held posts at Leipzig, Rostock, Basel, Jena (~1913–1924), Bonn (~1924–1926), and Munich (~1926–1939).

Ferdinand de Saussure (1857–1913) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Geneva, Leipzig, and Berlin. He was a Maître de Conférences at École Pratique des Hautes Études (1880–1891) and Professor at the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University (~2016–2018) under doctoral supervisor Aleksandra Wenta.

Fernando Tola (1915–2017) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the National University of San Marcos, he became a Professor at the University of Buenos Aires and directed the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).

Filipp Fortunatov (1848–1914) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Imperial Moscow University and under Georg Curtius and August Leskien, later holding a academic post at Imperial Moscow University/Moscow State University (~1876–1902).
